headline: European wireless and electronics is in a policy-driven upswing: 6G is being pulled forward to about 2029, Nokia's network business is growing on AI demand, and the Chips Act 2.0 is moving through the EU legislative process, while Finnish photonics and sensor startups keep raising seed rounds.
outlook_reason: 6G timelines, EU photonics and chip calls, and Finnish deep-tech funding rounds all point upward, though the Chips Act 2.0 has no new headline budget and Nokia's shares fell about 10% after its Q3 report.

signals.title: Helsinki summit: commercial 6G could arrive in 2029
signals.detail: Industry speakers at a 6G summit in Helsinki said the first commercial 6G networks are now expected in 2029, two years earlier than planned. Non-terrestrial networks (satellites) become part of the radio access itself.

signals.title: Ericsson and Telia Sweden sign 6G MoU
signals.detail: The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding to speed up 6G development, per eeNews Europe's coverage. I did not open the original article.

signals.title: SNS JU funds five new 6G projects (about €22M)
signals.detail: The projects include HEMES-6G, a large-scale experimentation platform across eight testbed sites in six EU countries. The date is approximate, taken from a search summary.

signals.title: Nokia Q3: AI and cloud drive growth, shares fall about 10%
signals.detail: Group sales were €5.15B (+10%). AI and cloud customer sales grew 123%, and the 2026 Network Infrastructure growth outlook was raised to 12–14%. Shares still dropped almost 10% in Helsinki on the day.

signals.title: Commission adopts Chips Act 2.0 proposal
signals.detail: The proposal (2026/0139(COD)) adds strategic projects, demand accelerators, expanded pilot lines and a Semiconductor Region of Excellence label, and favours procurement of local startup chips. It has no new headline funding figure. A Council debate was planned for 24 September 2026. It is older than 30 days but is the main regulatory item in the sector.

signals.title: Aalto metacrystal panels for 6G
signals.detail: Aalto researchers reported passive 3D-printed panels that guide wireless signals without electronics or power. The date is approximate (June 2026). This is research, not yet a company.

signals.title: Vexlum raises €10M
signals.detail: The Tampere-based semiconductor laser maker raised funding to scale chip and laser manufacturing. It may be the largest Nordic photonics seed round. The date is that of the article.
